choices.text: A diploid ovum from meiotic failure was fertilized by one sperm

choices.label: B
choices.text: A normal ovum was fertilized by one sperm, then lost a set

choices.label: C
choices.text: A normal ovum was fertilized by two sperm at once

choices.label: D
choices.text: An empty ovum was fertilized by one sperm that then duplicated

choices.label: E
choices.text: An ovum duplicated its own genome without sperm contribution

explanation.summary: A complete mole lacks the maternal genome: an empty ovum is fertilized by one sperm that undergoes mitosis (or by two sperm), usually giving 46,XX.
explanation.whyCorrect: A complete mole forms when the maternal genome is absent. Most often a single sperm fertilizes an empty ovum and duplicates by mitosis, producing a diploid, entirely paternal 46,XX conceptus with no fetal parts; less often two sperm fertilize the empty ovum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A diploid ovum plus a sperm would give a triploid conceptus containing maternal DNA, not a purely paternal diploid mole.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is not a mechanism the lecture describes, and it would not produce a genome that is entirely paternal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Two sperm fertilizing a normal ovum produces a triploid partial mole (69 chromosomes) with maternal DNA and fetal parts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Complete moles have no maternal genome; this scenario would be entirely maternal, the opposite of what cytogenetics shows.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman undergoes uterine evacuation after an ultrasound at 12 weeks shows a fetus with an abnormal, focally cystic placenta. Pathology shows two populations of villi, small fibrotic villi and scattered edematous hydropic villi, with focal trophoblastic hyperplasia and nucleated fetal erythrocytes in villous vessels. Which of the following additional findings is most expected in this tissue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diffuse, circumferential hyperplasia of all trophoblast

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diploid karyotype composed only of paternal chromosomes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nests of mononucleated cells splitting myometrial fibers

choices.label: D
choices.text: p57 staining in cytotrophoblast and stromal cell nuclei

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheets of cytotrophoblast with no villi in the specimen

explanation.summary: Partial moles are p57-positive in villous cytotrophoblast and stromal nuclei because they contain maternal genetic material.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two villous populations, limited trophoblastic hyperplasia, and fetal erythrocytes describe a partial mole. Because a partial mole arises from a normal ovum fertilized by two sperm, it carries maternal DNA, which immunohistochemistry reveals as p57 positivity in villous cytotrophoblast and stromal nuclei.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Diffuse, marked trophoblastic hyperplasia with uniformly edematous villi is the complete-mole pattern; partial moles have fewer hyperplastic trophoblasts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A diploid, all-paternal genome describes a complete mole; partial moles are triploid and include a maternal set.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mononucleated intermediate trophoblast splitting the myometrium is the picture of placental site trophoblastic tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trophoblast sheets without villi define choriocarcinoma, not a partial mole, which has villi.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman at 11 weeks' gestation has heavy sweating, palpitations, and a 4-kg weight loss. Her pulse is 124/min. Ultrasound shows a heterogeneous intrauterine mass with multiple cystic spaces and no fetus. Serum hCG is 240,000 mIU/mL, TSH is suppressed, and free T4 is elevated. Which of the following best explains her thyroid findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoantibodies that stimulate the thyrotropin receptor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct secretion of free T4 by the proliferating trophoblast

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen-driven increase in thyroxine-binding globulin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human placental lactogen stimulating thyroid follicular cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Weak activation of TSH receptors by structurally similar hCG

explanation.summary: Markedly elevated hCG from a molar pregnancy weakly activates TSH receptors, causing clinical hyperthyroidism.
explanation.whyCorrect: hCG is structurally similar to TSH. At the marked elevations seen with molar pregnancy, hCG weakly stimulates TSH receptors, producing hyperthyroidism with perspiration, weight loss, and tachycardia, while pituitary TSH is suppressed by feedback.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Receptor-stimulating autoantibodies describe an autoimmune thyroid process; the lecture attributes molar hyperthyroidism to hCG itself.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Trophoblast produces hCG, not thyroid hormone; the free T4 comes from the stimulated thyroid gland.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A rise in binding globulin changes total, not free, hormone and would not cause suppressed TSH with thyrotoxic symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hPL is the marker associated with placental site trophoblastic tumor; it is not the hormone that cross-reacts with TSH receptors.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman had a spontaneous abortion 5 months ago. She now has irregular vaginal bleeding and a markedly elevated serum hCG. A hemorrhagic, necrotic mass is found invading the uterine wall and is biopsied. Which of the following histologic findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chorionic villi embedded within the invaded myometrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enlarged hydropic villi with circumferential trophoblast

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mixed small fibrotic and hydropic villi with fetal cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mononucleated cells with uniform nuclei, splitting muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheets of cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast, no villi

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma consists of sheets of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts with hemorrhage and necrosis, and no chorionic villi.
explanation.whyCorrect: A hemorrhagic, necrotic uterine mass with very high hCG after a nonmolar pregnancy suggests choriocarcinoma. Histologically it is composed of sheets of the two placental cell types, pale cytotrophoblasts and dark multinucleate syncytiotrophoblasts, with mitoses and hemorrhage; unlike moles, villi are not evident.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Villi within invaded myometrium define an invasive mole; the absence of villi separates choriocarcinoma from it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hydropic villi with circumferential trophoblastic hyperplasia describe a complete mole, which contains villi.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Two populations of villi with fetal cells describe a partial mole.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uniform mononucleated intermediate trophoblast splitting smooth muscle is placental site trophoblastic tumor, which has low hCG.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is diagnosed with a complete hydatidiform mole at 9 weeks' gestation. She is hemodynamically stable, her hCG is 60,000 mIU/mL, and she hopes to have children in the future. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Expectant management with a repeat ultrasound in 4 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Methotrexate as the sole treatment, without evacuation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multi-agent chemotherapy with etoposide and dactinomycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Suction curettage followed by serial serum hCG levels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Total hysterectomy with preservation of the ovaries

explanation.summary: Molar pregnancies are removed by suction curettage, followed by serial hCG monitoring until normalization.
explanation.whyCorrect: A molar pregnancy should be treated promptly, typically by suction curettage. Afterward, serial hCG measurements continue until normalization and through a surveillance period, during which pregnancy is avoided so rising hCG can be interpreted.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Treatment should begin once a mole is detected to prevent further symptoms; observation is inappropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Methotrexate is added prophylactically for high-risk moles, not used alone in place of evacuation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Multi-agent regimens are used for choriocarcinoma, not first-line for an uncomplicated mole.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hysterectomy is an option only for a patient who does not plan to become pregnant again; this patient wants future children.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman delivered a healthy term infant 7 months ago. She now has irregular vaginal bleeding and a markedly elevated serum hCG, and evaluation shows a hemorrhagic uterine tumor composed of trophoblast without villi. Staging is planned. Which of the following sites is most likely to harbor metastatic disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Brain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kidney

choices.label: D
choices.text: Liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lungs

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma metastasizes most commonly to the lungs (about 50%), then the vagina (30%-40%).
explanation.whyCorrect: This is choriocarcinoma after a normal gestation. It metastasizes early and often; the lungs are the most common site (about 50%), where lesions cause hemoptysis and appear as cannonball masses on chest x-ray.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone is among the less common metastatic sites.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The brain is a less common site than the lungs and vagina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The kidney is among the less common metastatic sites.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The liver is listed among the less common metastatic sites of choriocarcinoma.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has had amenorrhea for 14 months since an uncomplicated term delivery. Serum hCG is only mildly elevated, and serum human placental lactogen is increased. Imaging shows a well-circumscribed 5-cm uterine mass with no evidence of spread beyond the uterus. Biopsy shows nests of mononucleated cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm infiltrating between smooth muscle fibers. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hysterectomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Multi-agent etoposide and dactinomycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Observation with serial hCG levels

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single-agent methotrexate chemotherapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suction curettage

explanation.summary: Placental site trophoblastic tumor is treated primarily surgically, most commonly by hysterectomy for localized disease; chemotherapy is less effective.
explanation.whyCorrect: Elevated hPL with a comparatively low hCG, a circumscribed mass, and intermediate trophoblast splitting the myometrium after a normal pregnancy indicate a placental site trophoblastic tumor. Unlike other gestational trophoblastic neoplasms, it responds less well to chemotherapy, so hysterectomy is the main treatment for localized disease.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Multi-agent chemotherapy is used for choriocarcinoma, which is extremely chemo-sensitive, unlike PSTT.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG is relatively low in PSTT and a subset behave aggressively; localized disease should be removed surgically.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Single-agent methotrexate suits early choriocarcinoma or high-risk moles; chemotherapy is less effective for PSTT.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Suction curettage evacuates molar tissue but does not treat a tumor that infiltrates the myometrium.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman underwent suction curettage for a complete mole 10 weeks ago. Her serum hCG initially fell, then plateaued and began to rise, and she has recurrent vaginal bleeding. A hysterectomy specimen shows hydropic chorionic villi with proliferating trophoblast penetrating deep into the myometrium and its vessels. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Choriocarcinoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Incomplete abortion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Invasive mole

choices.label: D
choices.text: Partial hydatidiform mole

choices.label: E
choices.text: Placental site trophoblastic tumor

explanation.summary: An invasive mole is a persistent molar gestation that invades the myometrium and its blood supply; villi remain evident.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 15% of complete moles progress to an invasive mole, which presents with vaginal bleeding and persistently elevated hCG after evacuation. Microscopically villi are still present within the invaded myometrium, which separates it from choriocarcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Choriocarcinoma also follows complete moles, but villi are not evident on its pathology.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An incomplete abortion does not produce rising hCG with villi invading the myometrium and vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A partial mole contains fetal tissue and a mix of normal and hydropic villi; it is not defined by myometrial invasion after evacuation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PSTT consists of intermediate trophoblast without hydropic villi and has relatively low hCG.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 11 weeks' gestation has vaginal bleeding and persistent nausea and vomiting. Her uterus is palpable well above the size expected for her dates, and serum hCG is 190,000 mIU/mL. Which of the following transvaginal ultrasound findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Empty uterus with a complex adnexal mass and free fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fetus with focal cystic change in an otherwise normal placenta

choices.label: C
choices.text: Live fetus with a normal-appearing, homogeneous placenta

choices.label: D
choices.text: Snowstorm pattern of cystic spaces with no fetal parts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Well-circumscribed solid mass infiltrating the myometrium

explanation.summary: A complete mole shows a snowstorm or bunch-of-grapes pattern with no fetal parts on ultrasound, reflecting cystic dilation of chorionic villi.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bleeding, hyperemesis, a uterus larger than dates, and hCG above 100,000 mIU/mL point to a complete mole. It is readily detected on ultrasound because no fetal parts are present, and the cystically dilated villi produce the characteristic snowstorm appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An empty uterus with an adnexal mass suggests ectopic pregnancy, not a molar gestation that enlarges the uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fetal parts with focal cystic placental change fit a partial mole, which usually has hCG closer to the normal pregnancy range.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A normal intrauterine pregnancy would not explain excess uterine size with hCG this high.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A solid, circumscribed myometrial mass is more typical of placental site trophoblastic tumor, which has low hCG.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman who has never been pregnant presents with pelvic pain and is found to have an ovarian mass and a markedly elevated serum hCG. Resection shows sheets of cytotrophoblast and multinucleate syncytiotrophoblast with extensive hemorrhage and no villi. Which of the following findings would best establish that this tumor is not of gestational origin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of chorionic villi anywhere in the tumor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of paternally derived DNA in tumor cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Extensive hemorrhage and necrosis in the gross specimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Presence of both cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum hCG level above 100,000 mIU/mL

explanation.summary: Nongestational choriocarcinomas are morphologically identical to gestational ones but lack paternally derived DNA, which all gestational choriocarcinomas contain.
explanation.whyCorrect: A small percentage of choriocarcinomas arise in the ovary or testis as germ cell tumors. They look the same microscopically as gestational choriocarcinoma, so morphology cannot separate them; the distinguishing feature is the absence of paternally derived DNA, which is present in every gestational choriocarcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lack of villi is shared by all choriocarcinomas and does not indicate origin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemorrhage and necrosis are gross features of choriocarcinoma generally, not markers of nongestational origin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both gestational and nongestational choriocarcinomas are made of the two trophoblast types; they are morphologically identical.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Markedly elevated hCG occurs with choriocarcinoma of either origin.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is seen 1 week after suction curettage for a complete hydatidiform mole. She is recovering well and asks when she can try to conceive again. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoid pregnancy during hCG surveillance so a rise can be interpreted

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid pregnancy permanently, since future gestations are contraindicated

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conceive after one normal hCG level, since surveillance then stops

choices.label: D
choices.text: Conceive once bleeding stops, since hCG testing is only done if symptoms recur

choices.label: E
choices.text: Try to conceive right away, since hCG is not followed after evacuation

explanation.summary: After molar evacuation, serial hCG is followed until normalization and through a surveillance period, during which pregnancy is avoided so hCG results remain accurate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serial hCG monitoring is required after evacuation until normalization and for an additional surveillance period. A new pregnancy would raise hCG and mask persistent or malignant trophoblastic disease, so the patient should avoid pregnancy during this time; afterward, successful pregnancy is possible.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pregnancy is not permanently contraindicated; many patients go on to have healthy pregnancies after surveillance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Monitoring continues beyond normalization for an additional surveillance period, not just until one normal level.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Surveillance is routine and scheduled, not symptom-triggered, because transformation can be silent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG must be followed after evacuation; an immediate pregnancy would confound that surveillance.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman develops hemoptysis and rising hCG 3 months after evacuation of a complete mole. Chest x-ray shows multiple circumscribed pulmonary masses, and imaging also shows liver lesions. Biopsy shows trophoblast without villi. She wishes to preserve her fertility. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hysterectomy alone, because chemotherapy is largely ineffective

choices.label: B
choices.text: Multi-agent chemotherapy with curative intent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Palliative care, because widely metastatic disease is incurable

choices.label: D
choices.text: Radiation to the lung masses, then serial hCG levels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat suction curettage, then observation with hCG

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma is extremely chemo-sensitive; even widely metastatic disease can be cured with chemotherapy, often preserving fertility.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is metastatic choriocarcinoma after a complete mole. Early disease is treated with single-agent methotrexate, and more extensive disease with multi-agent regimens that may include etoposide and dactinomycin. Because the tumor is extremely chemo-sensitive, cure is possible even with wide metastases, and fertility can be preserved in many patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Poor chemo-responsiveness describes placental site trophoblastic tumor, not choriocarcinoma; hysterectomy alone also sacrifices fertility.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metastatic choriocarcinoma is often curable, so a palliative-only approach is inappropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation is not the treatment the lecture describes; systemic chemotherapy addresses widespread disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Curettage treats molar pregnancy; it does not address metastatic choriocarcinoma.

questions.stem: In a normal early pregnancy, trophoblastic cells of the chorionic villi secrete human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG). Which of the following is the principal way this hormone sustains early pregnancy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stimulating endometrial gland secretion of glycogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stimulating fetal adrenal production of cortisol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stimulating maternal pituitary release of prolactin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stimulating ovarian follicle recruitment and growth

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stimulating progesterone production by the corpus luteum

explanation.summary: Trophoblast-derived hCG sustains early pregnancy by stimulating progesterone production in the corpus luteum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trophoblasts of the chorionic villi produce hCG, which is vital in sustaining early pregnancy through stimulation of progesterone production in the corpus luteum. This is also why hCG is the key laboratory marker for trophoblastic proliferation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: hCG's pregnancy-sustaining role is exerted on the corpus luteum, not directly on endometrial glands.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fetal adrenal cortisol production is not the mechanism by which hCG sustains early pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG does not act by stimulating pituitary prolactin release.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Follicle recruitment is not how hCG maintains pregnancy; its target is the corpus luteum.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman's first-trimester evacuation specimen contains fetal tissue, and the placenta shows some villi of normal size alongside scattered hydropic villi with mild trophoblastic hyperplasia. Cytogenetic analysis is performed. Which of the following karyotypes is most likely?

choices.label: B
choices.text: 46,XX

choices.label: C
choices.text: 46,XY

choices.label: D
choices.text: 47,XXY

choices.label: E
choices.text: 69,XXY

explanation.summary: A partial mole arises from two sperm fertilizing one ovum and is triploid (69,XXX, 69,XXY, or 69,XYY).
explanation.whyCorrect: Fetal tissue plus a mix of normal and hydropic villi indicates a partial mole. Dispermic fertilization of a normal ovum yields one maternal and two paternal haploid sets, a triploid karyotype such as 69,XXY.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 45,X is a monosomy unrelated to molar pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 46,XX is the most common karyotype of a complete mole, which has no fetal parts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 46,XY is the less common complete-mole karyotype, again with no fetal tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 47,XXY is a single extra chromosome, not the triploidy of a partial mole.

questions.stem: A pathologist is evaluating a molar specimen with uniformly edematous villi, marked trophoblastic hyperplasia arranged in clusters, and no fetal tissue. p57 immunohistochemistry is performed on the villous cytotrophoblast nuclei. Which of the following is the expected result and its explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Negative, because the maternal genome is entirely absent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Negative, because the tissue carries three chromosome sets

choices.label: C
choices.text: Positive, because a maternal chromosome set is present

choices.label: D
choices.text: Positive, because fetal erythrocytes occupy villous vessels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Positive, because the paternal chromosomes are duplicated

explanation.summary: p57 staining signals maternal genetic material; a complete mole, which lacks the maternal genome, does not show it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uniformly edematous villi, clustered trophoblastic hyperplasia, and no fetal tissue indicate a complete mole. p57 positivity in villous cytotrophoblast and stromal nuclei shows that maternal genetic material is present, as in partial moles; a complete mole has no maternal genome, so p57 staining is expected to be absent.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Three chromosome sets describe a triploid partial mole; the complete mole is diploid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A maternal chromosome set with p57 positivity is the partial-mole situation, not this complete mole.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fetal erythrocytes are absent in complete moles, and p57 reflects maternal DNA, not fetal red cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Duplicated paternal chromosomes are the basis of a complete mole but do not produce p57 positivity, which reflects maternal DNA.

questions.stem: Each of the following women is newly pregnant. Based on maternal age alone, which of them has the highest risk of a molar pregnancy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 17-year-old woman

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 23-year-old woman

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 26-year-old woman

choices.label: D
choices.text: A 29-year-old woman

choices.label: E
choices.text: A 33-year-old woman

explanation.summary: Molar pregnancy risk is highest at the two ends of reproductive life: teenagers and women aged 40 to 50.
explanation.whyCorrect: Molar pregnancies can occur at any age, but risk is higher at the extremes of reproductive life, in teenagers and between 40 and 50 years of age. Of the options, only the teenager falls into a higher-risk group.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Age 23 is in the middle of reproductive life, where risk is lower than at the extremes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Age 26 is mid-reproductive age and not a higher-risk group.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Age 29 is mid-reproductive age and not a higher-risk group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Age 33 is below the 40-50 higher-risk range.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman's molar evacuation specimen is diploid, and every chromosome is of paternal origin. Which of the following histologic descriptions best fits this specimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delicate villous stroma with a two-layer trophoblast cover

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mononucleated eosinophilic cells splitting smooth muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Numerous large edematous villi with hyperplastic trophoblast

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sheets of biphasic trophoblast without any villi present

choices.label: E
choices.text: Small fibrotic villi mixed with hydropic villi and fetal cells

explanation.summary: A complete mole shows villi that are more edematous and numerous, with hyperplastic trophoblast in clusters and no fetal tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: A diploid, entirely paternal genome identifies a complete mole. Histologically it looks more pathologic than a partial mole: large, widely spaced edematous villi, abundant hyperplastic trophoblast surrounding the villi, and no fetal tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Delicate stroma covered by syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblast describes normal first-trimester villi.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mononucleated cells splitting smooth muscle describe placental site trophoblastic tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trophoblast sheets without villi describe choriocarcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Two villous populations with fetal cells describe a partial mole, which is triploid with a maternal set.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman at 13 weeks' gestation has light vaginal bleeding. Ultrasound shows a fetus without cardiac activity, and her serum hCG is within the range expected for her gestational age. She is managed as an incomplete abortion, and pathology later reveals a partial mole. Which of the following features most contributed to the missed diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A diploid karyotype identical to that of normal pregnancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: A snowstorm pattern mistaken for uterine fibroids

choices.label: C
choices.text: Absence of any vaginal bleeding before the procedure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fetal parts on imaging and a non-elevated hCG

choices.label: E
choices.text: hCG above 100,000 mIU/mL mistaken for a twin gestation

explanation.summary: Partial moles are easily missed because they contain fetal parts and have hCG levels closer to normal for pregnancy, mimicking an incomplete or complete abortion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike a complete mole, a partial mole contains fetal parts, so ultrasound can mimic a failed pregnancy. Its hCG is also closer to normal for pregnancy rather than extremely elevated, so the diagnosis can be missed unless other clinical features are considered with imaging.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Partial moles are triploid, not diploid, and karyotype is not available when the clinical diagnosis is made.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The snowstorm pattern is characteristic of a complete mole, which lacks fetal parts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The patient did bleed; vaginal bleeding is a common presentation of molar pregnancy and is not what hides the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Very high hCG is typical of complete moles; this patient's hCG was near the expected range.

questions.stem: A histology student examines first-trimester chorionic villi. Each villus has a delicate stromal core covered by two epithelial layers. Which cell type forms the outer layer of this covering?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cytotrophoblast

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decidual stromal cell

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intermediate trophoblast

choices.label: D
choices.text: Syncytiotrophoblast

choices.label: E
choices.text: Villous endothelial cell

explanation.summary: First-trimester villi have an outer syncytiotrophoblast layer and an inner cytotrophoblast layer around a delicate stroma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Normal first-trimester chorionic villi consist of a delicate mesh of central stroma surrounded by two epithelial layers: the outer syncytiotrophoblast and the inner cytotrophoblast.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytotrophoblast forms the inner, not outer, epithelial layer of the villus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Decidual cells are maternal endometrial cells, not part of the villous epithelium.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intermediate trophoblast anchors the placenta to the endometrium and gives rise to PSTT; it is not the villous surface layer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endothelial cells line the capillaries within the villous stroma, not its outer covering.

questions.stem: Placental tissue from a term delivery is compared with first-trimester placental tissue under the microscope. Which of the following features characterizes the villi from the term placenta?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Circumferential trophoblastic hyperplasia around each villus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delicate loose stroma with a thick two-layer trophoblast

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dense dilated capillaries with thinned trophoblast layers

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hydropic, cistern-like stroma with no blood vessels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of trophoblast with fibrin replacing the stroma

explanation.summary: Third-trimester villi show a dense network of dilated capillaries surrounded by thinned-out syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblast layers.
explanation.whyCorrect: As the placenta matures, the villous stroma develops a more dense network of dilated capillaries, and the overlying syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblast layers become thinned out, in contrast to the delicate stroma and two distinct layers of first-trimester villi.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Circumferential trophoblastic hyperplasia is a feature of complete moles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A delicate stroma with a distinct two-layer trophoblast describes first-trimester villi.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hydropic villi without normal vasculature suggest a molar process, not a normal term placenta.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lecture describes thinned trophoblast layers, not loss of trophoblast with fibrin replacement.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman with a high-risk complete mole receives a prophylactic folic acid analog after suction curettage. This drug acts by competitively inhibiting which of the following enzymes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dihydrofolate reductase

choices.label: B
choices.text: DNA polymerase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ribonucleotide reductase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thymidylate synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topoisomerase II

explanation.summary: Methotrexate is a folic acid analog that competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, preventing cell growth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Methotrexate, used prophylactically for high-risk moles and to treat choriocarcinoma, is an antitumor folic acid analog. It competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, which prevents cell growth.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DNA polymerase is not methotrexate's competitive target.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ribonucleotide reductase is not methotrexate's target.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thymidylate synthase is not the enzyme the lecture identifies as methotrexate's target.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Topoisomerase II is not inhibited by this folic acid analog.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman receives several doses of methotrexate for gestational trophoblastic disease. Two weeks later she has painful oral ulcers and pancytopenia. In addition to mucositis and myelosuppression, this drug is known to cause which of the following adverse effects?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dilated cardiomyopathy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemorrhagic cystitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peripheral neuropathy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pulmonary fibrosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sensorineural hearing loss

explanation.summary: Methotrexate's major adverse effects include pulmonary fibrosis, myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and mucositis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture lists methotrexate's major adverse effects as pulmonary fibrosis, myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and mucositis. Her ulcers and cytopenias reflect mucositis and myelosuppression; pulmonary fibrosis is the other listed toxicity among the options.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cardiomyopathy is not among methotrexate's listed adverse effects.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemorrhagic cystitis is not among methotrexate's listed adverse effects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Peripheral neuropathy is not among methotrexate's listed adverse effects.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hearing loss is not among methotrexate's listed adverse effects.

questions.stem: A resident reviewing a series of patients with gestational choriocarcinoma notes the type of pregnancy that preceded each tumor. Approximately what proportion of gestational choriocarcinomas are derived from complete hydatidiform moles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 2.5%

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 15%

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 50%

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 85%

choices.label: E
choices.text: Essentially 100%

explanation.summary: About half of choriocarcinomas derive from complete moles; the other half follow normal pregnancies, spontaneous abortions, and ectopic pregnancies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Approximately 50% of choriocarcinomas are derived from complete hydatidiform moles, and the other 50% arise from other pregnancies such as normal gestations, spontaneous abortions, and ectopic pregnancies. A molar pregnancy is 100 times more likely than other gestations to give rise to choriocarcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: About 2.5% is the risk that a complete mole progresses to choriocarcinoma, not the share of choriocarcinomas that come from moles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 15% is the fraction of complete moles that become invasive moles.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Half of choriocarcinomas follow nonmolar pregnancies, so the proportion is far below 85%.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Choriocarcinoma also follows normal, ectopic, and aborted pregnancies, so it is not exclusively molar.

questions.stem: A uterine tumor from a woman with rapidly rising hCG is composed of sheets of two trophoblast cell types with prominent mitoses and hemorrhage. One population consists of individual cells with pale, clear cytoplasm; the other consists of large multinucleate cells with dark, shaded cytoplasm. Which of the following are the multinucleate cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cytotrophoblasts

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decidualized stromal cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intermediate trophoblasts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Syncytiotrophoblasts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Villous stromal cells

explanation.summary: In choriocarcinoma, cytotrophoblasts are individual cells with pale (clear) cytoplasm, and syncytiotrophoblasts are multinucleate cells with dark (shaded) cytoplasm.
explanation.whyCorrect: Choriocarcinoma consists of sheets of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts. The multinucleate cells with dark cytoplasm are syncytiotrophoblasts, while the individual pale-staining cells are cytotrophoblasts.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytotrophoblasts are the individual cells with pale, clear cytoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Decidual cells are maternal endometrial cells and are not a component of the tumor's biphasic sheets.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intermediate trophoblast is mononucleated and forms PSTT, not the biphasic pattern of choriocarcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Choriocarcinoma lacks villi, so villous stromal cells are not part of its histology.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman is being staged for choriocarcinoma that followed an ectopic pregnancy. Chest imaging already shows pulmonary nodules. Apart from the lungs, which of the following is the most common site of metastasis for this tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Brain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kidney

choices.label: D
choices.text: Liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vagina

explanation.summary: After the lungs (about 50%), the vagina (30%-40%) is the next most common site of choriocarcinoma metastasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Choriocarcinoma metastasizes early and often. The most common sites are the lungs (about 50%) and the vagina (30%-40%); the brain, liver, bone, and kidney are less common.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone is a less common metastatic site than the vagina.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The brain is a less common metastatic site than the vagina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The kidney is a less common metastatic site than the vagina.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The liver is a less common metastatic site than the vagina.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman who delivered a healthy infant 9 months ago presents with cough, hemoptysis, and irregular vaginal bleeding. Chest x-ray shows multiple round, well-circumscribed masses in both lungs. Serum hCG is markedly elevated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Choriocarcinoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete hydatidiform mole

choices.label: C
choices.text: Invasive mole

choices.label: D
choices.text: Partial hydatidiform mole

choices.label: E
choices.text: Placental site trophoblastic tumor

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma can follow a normal pregnancy and often presents already metastatic, with hemoptysis and cannonball lung lesions and markedly elevated hCG.
explanation.whyCorrect: Half of choriocarcinomas arise after nonmolar pregnancies, where they are harder to detect clinically; they grow rapidly and are often metastatic at diagnosis. Lung metastases cause hemoptysis and cannonball lesions on chest x-ray, and hCG is markedly elevated.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A complete mole is a molar gestation, not a postpartum metastatic tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An invasive mole follows evacuation of a molar pregnancy, which this patient did not have.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A partial mole is a molar pregnancy with fetal parts, not a disease presenting months after a healthy delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PSTT also most often follows a normal pregnancy and can reach the lungs, but its hCG is much lower than in other GTD.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is receiving chemotherapy for persistent molar tissue that has invaded the myometrium after evacuation of a complete mole; villi were identified on biopsy. She suddenly develops severe abdominal pain, hypotension, and a falling hematocrit. Which of the following complications has most likely occurred?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ovarian torsion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pulmonary embolism

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ruptured ectopic pregnancy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thyroid storm

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterine rupture

explanation.summary: An invasive mole responds well to chemotherapy but can cause uterine rupture, necessitating hysterectomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: An invasive mole persists by invading the myometrium and its blood supply. Although it responds well to chemotherapy, deep invasion can lead to uterine rupture, presenting with acute pain and hemorrhage, and may necessitate hysterectomy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ovarian torsion is not the complication the lecture ties to myometrial invasion by molar tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A pulmonary embolism would not explain acute abdominal pain with blood loss.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Her hCG source is known persistent molar tissue, not a new ectopic gestation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thyroid storm would not produce acute hemorrhage with a falling hematocrit.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman has just undergone suction curettage for a complete hydatidiform mole. She asks which outcome is most likely to require further treatment. Of the following, which is the most frequent sequela after evacuation of a complete mole?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Choriocarcinoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Invasive mole

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nongestational germ cell tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Placental site trophoblastic tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recurrent partial mole

explanation.summary: About 15% of complete moles progress to invasive mole, whereas only about 2.5% progress to choriocarcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Around 15% of patients with a complete mole develop an invasive mole, in which molar tissue persists and invades the myometrium. Progression to choriocarcinoma is much rarer, with about a 2.5% risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Choriocarcinoma follows about 2.5% of complete moles, far less often than invasive mole.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nongestational choriocarcinomas are gonadal germ cell tumors unrelated to prior pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PSTT is rare (about 3% of GTD) and most commonly arises after normal pregnancy, not molar pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A partial mole is a separate fertilization event, not a sequela of evacuating a complete mole.

questions.stem: A placental site trophoblastic tumor is composed of intermediate trophoblast, a distinct form of trophoblast derived from cytotrophoblasts. In a normal pregnancy, which of the following is the principal role of this cell type?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anchoring the placenta to the maternal endometrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forming the finger-like projections of the villi

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forming the outer syncytial covering of the villi

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lining the capillaries within the villous stroma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Producing progesterone in the corpus luteum

explanation.summary: Intermediate trophoblast, derived from cytotrophoblasts, anchors the placenta to the maternal endometrium and is the tissue of origin of PSTT.
explanation.whyCorrect: PSTT is made of intermediate trophoblastic tissue, which originates from cytotrophoblasts and serves to anchor the placenta to the maternal endometrium; PSTTs arise from the site where the placenta is anchored.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The villi themselves are chorionic projections for nutrient exchange; intermediate trophoblast anchors the placenta.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The outer villous covering is syncytiotrophoblast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Villous capillaries are lined by endothelium, not trophoblast.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The corpus luteum is a maternal ovarian structure stimulated by hCG, not a trophoblast derivative.

questions.stem: A pathologist diagnoses a placental site trophoblastic tumor in a hysterectomy specimen and reviews the patient's obstetric history. After which of the following types of pregnancy does this tumor most commonly arise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete molar pregnancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ectopic pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal pregnancy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Partial molar pregnancy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spontaneous abortion

explanation.summary: PSTT can follow abortion, molar, ectopic, or normal pregnancy, but most commonly arises after a normal pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Placental site trophoblastic tumors can occur after an abortion, molar pregnancy, normal pregnancy, or ectopic pregnancy; however, they most commonly arise after a normal pregnancy, not a molar pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Complete moles are the leading antecedent of choriocarcinoma, but PSTT most commonly follows normal pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ectopic pregnancy is a possible but less common antecedent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PSTT can follow molar pregnancy but is not most commonly associated with it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Abortion is a possible but less common antecedent.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman has painless intermittent vaginal bleeding beginning 2 years after an uncomplicated delivery. Ultrasound shows a solid uterine mass. Her serum hCG is elevated but far lower than expected for a trophoblastic tumor of this size. Which of the following serum markers is most likely to be increased and support the suspected diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alpha-fetoprotein

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cancer antigen 125

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human placental lactogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibin A

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lactate dehydrogenase

explanation.summary: PSTT is characterized by increased serum hPL with hCG levels much lower than in other forms of GTD.
explanation.whyCorrect: A slow-growing uterine tumor presenting with painless bleeding years after a normal pregnancy, with disproportionately low hCG, suggests placental site trophoblastic tumor. Serum human placental lactogen is increased in PSTT, while hCG is much lower than in other GTD.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alpha-fetoprotein is not the marker the lecture associates with PSTT.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CA-125 is not a marker of trophoblastic tumors in this lecture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin is not the marker associated with intermediate trophoblast tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lactate dehydrogenase is nonspecific and not the characteristic PSTT marker.

questions.stem: A hysterectomy specimen contains a well-circumscribed 5-cm uterine mass with a solid tan-brown cut surface and focal hemorrhage. Microscopy shows sheets of mononucleated cells with uniform nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm infiltrating the myometrium and separating individual smooth muscle cells. No villi or multinucleate syncytial cells are present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete hydatidiform mole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gestational choriocarcinoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Invasive hydatidiform mole

choices.label: D
choices.text: Partial hydatidiform mole

choices.label: E
choices.text: Placental site trophoblastic tumor

explanation.summary: PSTT is a well-circumscribed, tan-brown mass of uniform mononucleated intermediate trophoblast that infiltrates and splits the myometrium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most PSTTs are well circumscribed, average about 5 cm, and have a solid tan-brown cut surface, often with hemorrhage and necrosis. Microscopically, sheets or nests of mononucleated cells with uniform nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm infiltrate the myometrium, splitting the smooth muscle cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A complete mole consists of numerous hydropic villi with hyperplastic trophoblast.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Choriocarcinoma is a yellow-white hemorrhagic tumor of biphasic cytotrophoblast and multinucleate syncytiotrophoblast.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An invasive mole shows villi within the myometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A partial mole shows normal and hydropic villi with fetal tissue.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman is diagnosed with a placental site trophoblastic tumor that is found to behave aggressively, with spread beyond the uterus. If distant metastases are present, which organ is most likely to be involved?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gastrointestinal tract

choices.label: B
choices.text: Liver

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lungs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pelvis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vagina

explanation.summary: About 10-15% of PSTTs are aggressive; their metastases most commonly involve the lungs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although most PSTTs are indolent, approximately 10-15% behave aggressively and can spread via lymphatics to near and distant organs. Metastases most commonly involve the lungs, though the liver, vagina, GI tract, pelvis, and other sites can be involved.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The GI tract can be involved but is less common than the lungs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The liver can be involved but is less common than the lungs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pelvis can be involved but is less common than the lungs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vagina can be involved but is less common than the lungs.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has just undergone suction curettage for a complete mole. Her uterine size matched her dates, and her pre-evacuation hCG was 70,000 mIU/mL. Her obstetric history is reviewed to decide whether prophylactic methotrexate is warranted. Which of the following historical features would place her at high risk for malignant transformation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prior cesarean delivery for breech presentation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prior hydatidiform mole in an earlier pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prior spontaneous vaginal term delivery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prior uncomplicated first-trimester miscarriage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prior use of combined oral contraceptives

explanation.summary: Risk factors for malignant transformation of a mole include advanced maternal age, excess uterine growth, hCG above 100,000 mIU/mL, and previous molar pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prophylactic chemotherapy such as methotrexate may be added for molar pregnancies at high risk of malignant transformation. The listed risk factors are advanced maternal age, excess uterine growth, hCG greater than 100,000 mIU/mL, and previous molar pregnancy. She has none of the first three, so a prior mole would be the qualifying feature.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Prior cesarean delivery is not a listed risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A prior normal delivery is not a listed risk factor for transformation of a mole.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A prior miscarriage is not a listed risk factor for molar transformation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral contraceptive use is not a listed risk factor.

questions.stem: Cytogenetic analysis of a complete hydatidiform mole shows a 46,XY karyotype with no maternal chromosomes. Which of the following mechanisms most likely produced this particular karyotype?

choices.label: A
choices.text: One sperm fertilized a normal ovum that then lost its nucleus

choices.label: B
choices.text: One X-bearing sperm fertilized an empty ovum and duplicated

choices.label: C
choices.text: One Y-bearing sperm fertilized an empty ovum and duplicated

choices.label: D
choices.text: Two sperm fertilized a normal ovum carrying an X chromosome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two sperm, one X- and one Y-bearing, fertilized an empty ovum

explanation.summary: Complete moles arise from an empty ovum fertilized either by one duplicating sperm (giving 46,XX) or by two sperm (dispermy), which can give 46,XY.
explanation.whyCorrect: Complete moles lack a maternal genome and form either when a single sperm fertilizes an empty ovum and undergoes mitosis, or when two sperm fertilize an empty ovum. A duplicated single sperm carries two copies of the same sex chromosome, so a 46,XY complete mole requires two different sperm, one X-bearing and one Y-bearing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is not a mechanism the lecture describes for complete moles; the ovum is empty from the outset.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Duplication of an X-bearing sperm gives 46,XX, the most common complete-mole karyotype, not 46,XY.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Duplication of a Y-bearing sperm would give two Y chromosomes and no X, not 46,XY.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Two sperm fertilizing a normal ovum produce a triploid partial mole containing maternal chromosomes.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman at 10 weeks' gestation has a molar pregnancy with an hCG of 210,000 mIU/mL. She reports palpitations, heat intolerance, and tremor, and her pulse is 118/min. Before evacuation, thyroid function tests are ordered. Which of the following results is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated TSH and elevated free T4

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elevated TSH and low free T4

choices.label: C
choices.text: Low TSH and elevated free T4

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low TSH and low free T4

choices.label: E
choices.text: Normal TSH and normal free T4

explanation.summary: hCG-driven hyperthyroidism in molar pregnancy produces elevated free T4 with suppressed TSH, so TSH should be checked in a symptomatic patient.
explanation.whyCorrect: Markedly elevated hCG weakly activates the thyroid's TSH receptors, increasing thyroid hormone output. The excess free T4 feeds back to suppress pituitary TSH, giving low TSH with elevated free T4, which is why TSH is checked in a molar patient with palpitations or weight loss.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The stimulus here is hCG acting at the thyroid, so pituitary TSH is suppressed rather than elevated.
whyWrongByChoice.B: High TSH with low free T4 is a hypothyroid pattern, the opposite of hCG-driven thyroid stimulation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Low TSH with low free T4 would suggest central hypothyroidism, not hCG-driven hyperthyroidism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Her symptoms and marked hCG elevation make normal thyroid tests unlikely.
